title: Element-site localization and canonical module restriction
statement: Let $C$ be a small category with Grothendieck topology $J$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and fix the common universe for its objects, morphisms, ring sections, set-sheaf sections and module fibres [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $R$ be a sheaf of rings and $A$ a sheaf of sets on $(C,J)$. The element site has underlying category $\operatorname{El}(A)^{\mathrm{op}}$, with objects $(U,s)$ for $s\in A(U)$ and arrows induced by restriction in $A$. Its projection $p_A$ sends $(U,s)$ to $U$. Define its topology $J_A$ to be the induced Grothendieck topology $p_A.\operatorname{inducedTopology}(J)$, and define $R_A=p_A^*R$ by precomposition with $p_A^{\mathrm{op}}$. On module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], define the canonical restriction $j_A^*:\operatorname{Mod}(R)\to\operatorname{Mod}(R_A)$ by precomposition along $p_A$ with identity coefficient map, so $(j_A^*M)(U,s)=M(U)$ and morphisms and restrictions are inherited sectionwise. A morphism of sheaves $b:B\to A$ induces the element functor $p_b:\operatorname{El}(B)^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{El}(A)^{\mathrm{op}}$, $(U,t)\mapsto(U,b_U(t))$. Given continuity of $p_b$ for $J_B,J_A$, define $j_b^*:\operatorname{Mod}(R_A)\to\operatorname{Mod}(R_B)$ by this same sectionwise restriction with identity coefficient map. These are the concrete element-site localization constructions, without an adjunction or equivalence assertion.
